steps.instruction: 洋葱切成约3.2毫米厚片。在一个大不锈钢汤锅，或两个大不锈钢/铸铁平底锅中，以中高火融化90克无盐黄油至起泡。加入洋葱，偶尔翻动，煮约8分钟至变软。转中低火，经常翻动，继续煮1至2小时，至洋葱十分甘甜、呈浓郁金棕色。若锅底褐色洋葱汁快焦，加入1汤匙（来源明确15毫升）水，刮起褐色附着物，再继续煮。用盐和黑胡椒调味。
加入干雪莉酒煮至微沸，同时刮起锅底褐色附着物。若用了两个平底锅，将雪莉酒分至两锅，再把两锅中的洋葱及液体刮入一个汤锅或荷兰锅。煮约3分钟，至酒精气味基本散去。加入高汤、百里香和月桂叶，升至中高火煮到微沸，再调低火煨20分钟。
加入苹果醋；如选用鱼露，此时一并加入。用盐和黑胡椒调味，弃去百里香枝和月桂叶。
将8片与碗口大小相称的乡村面包烤至酥脆。预热烤箱上火，烤架调至最上层。用另取的黄油涂烤面包片，再用蒜瓣擦至有香气。在4个可入烤箱的汤碗底各舀少量汤汁，各放入1片烤面包（先用其中4片），撒一些磨碎干酪。继续舀入汤和洋葱至接近碗满，再各放1片余下的烤面包，向下轻压至几乎浸入汤中。覆盖余下的干酪，将汤碗放在有边沿的烤盘上。用上火烤至干酪融化且局部呈棕色，撒细香葱，食用。

technique: 来源时长栏：准备20分钟，烹饪2小时，整道总用时2小时20分钟（140分钟）；4人份。
黄油慢煮洋葱至非常软、浓郁金棕色和甘甜，不要求焦到深褐甚至发苦。焦糖化1至2小时随锅具、批量与脂肪而变化；来源总时长明示140分钟，不用任一范围上限重新推算整道总时长。
原文提供大不锈钢汤锅或两只大不锈钢/铸铁平底锅；两锅方式先分雪莉酒，刮下并合并到汤锅或荷兰锅继续，未给两锅比例不得平分编造毫升数。
盐及黑胡椒在洋葱阶段和汤底完成阶段分次调味；锅底汁液快焦时用来源1汤匙（15毫升）水刮起，可随需要再用，不虚构全程总水量。
4个耐烤碗、有边沿烤盘、烤架最上层和上火烘烤是必要设备与操作；来源未给烤箱温度或焗烤分钟，保持未知。
8片酥脆面包分两层各4片，干酪第一层撒一些、顶部用余下的，分层干酪克数未明示。
tips: 黄洋葱最适合通用做法；黄洋葱、甜洋葱（如Vidalia）、红洋葱及红葱头混合可产生更复杂的风味，并非必须混用。
若没有自制牛高汤，来源建议自制或低钠市售鸡高汤；不要替换成未获同来源推荐的普通市售牛高汤。
来源文章说明雪莉酒可选味美思（vermouth）、白葡萄酒，也提到红葡萄酒或波特酒作为替代；未明确各替代用量，只作为可选替代说明，不改变本主配方120毫升干雪莉酒。
鱼露可选；苹果醋、雪莉酒用于增加汤底复杂度。
sources.rawExcerpt:
French Onion Soup (Soupe à l'Oignon Gratinée)
Here's the recipe you need to get the best caramelized onion- and cheese-filled flavor in every steamy, crouton-topped bowl of French onion soup.
By Daniel Gritzer
Updated on September 26, 2025
Why It Works
Caramelizing the onions slowly in butter until they're rich golden brown (but not so dark as to taste bitter) produces the sweetest, most flavorful results.
Using a mix of onions—sweet, yellow, red, and shallots—creates a well-rounded flavor, though great soup can be made with just one type.
If you don't have homemade beef stock, the recipe's suggested homemade or store-bought chicken stock substitutions are better than most store-bought beef stock.
Fish sauce, cider vinegar, and sherry add depth and complexity to the broth.
Caramelizing the Onions
Caramelization can be a wildly inconsistent process. Different pots and pans, batch sizes, and fats all change how (and how quickly) onions caramelize.
Yes, over high heat, onions can brown on the surface very quickly, especially in a pan that's not crowded. But the goal of caramelizing onions isn't just to brown the surface; it's to transform the onions so that they're soft and sweet to the core. Try to rush it and all you'll end up doing is burning them. Here's the skinny: Caramelizing onions, even to the lesser degree I'm advocating here, takes at least an hour, sometimes two.
Best Broth for French Onion Soup
With the onions caramelized, the next step is to add the liquid and simmer it all together. I start with some sherry, since I love that nutty, oxidized flavor with the caramelized onions. You could also use vermouth or white wine, and some folks even use red wine or port. Take your pick; they're all good.
While homemade beef stock is the very best option, there's no reason to turn your nose up at chicken stock, which is without a doubt the most versatile of all stocks to keep on hand in the kitchen. A great homemade chicken stock will produce an absolutely phenomenal French onion soup, and a good store-bought brand can still make a more than good enough version.
Finishing French Onion Soup
I start by buttering warm croutons and rubbing them with garlic.
Then I spoon a little of the soup into each (oven-safe) bowl. I set a crouton on top and top that with cheese.
Then I ladle in the bulk of the soup, nearly filling up each bowl. I add another crouton on top of that.
And finish it with a very generous grating of Gruyère cheese. I broil the soups until the cheese is melted and browned in spots, then top each one off with a garnish of minced chives, for a little hit of fresh onion flavor to play off the deep sweetness of the cooked onions.
Prep Time: 20 mins
Cook Time: 2 hrs
Total Time: 2 hrs 20 mins
Servings: 4 servings
Yield: Serves 4
Ingredients
6 tablespoons (90g) unsalted butter, plus more for bread
3 pounds (1.4kg) yellow or mixed onions, sliced 1/8 inch thick (see note)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste, divided
1/2 cup (120 ml) dry sherry (such as Amontillado)
2 quarts (1.8L) homemade beef stock or homemade or store-bought low-sodium chicken stock
2 sprigs thyme
1 bay leaf
1 teaspoon (5 ml) Fish sauce (optional)
1 teaspoon (5 ml) cider vinegar
8 bowl-size slices rustic bread, toasted until crisp
1 medium clove garlic
1 pound (450 g) Gruyère cheese, grated
2 tablespoons freshly minced chives, for garnish
Directions
1. In a large stainless steel saucepan, or in 2 large stainless steel or cast iron skillets, melt butter over medium-high heat until foaming. Add onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8 minutes. Lower heat to medium-low and cook, stirring frequently, until onions are very sweet and a rich golden-brown color, 1 to 2 hours. If browned onion juices on bottom of pot threaten to burn, add 1 tablespoon (15ml) water, scrape up browned bits, and continue cooking. Season with salt and pepper.
2. Add sherry and bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits. (If using 2 skillets, divide sherry between them, then scrape onions and liquid from both pans into a pot or Dutch oven to continue.) Cook until alcohol smell is mostly gone, about 3 minutes. Add stock, thyme, and bay leaf; raise heat to medium-high; and bring to a simmer. Lower heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
3. Add fish sauce, if using, and cider vinegar. Season with salt and pepper. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaf.
4. Preheat broiler and adjust oven rack to top position. Butter toasts and rub with garlic clove until fragrant. Spoon a small amount of broth into the bottoms of 4 ovenproof serving bowls, then top with half the toasts. Sprinkle some grated cheese on top of toasts, then spoon more soup and onions on top, nearly filling bowls. Set remaining 4 toasts in bowls, pushing to nearly submerge them. Top with remaining grated cheese and set bowls on a rimmed baking sheet. Broil until cheese is melted and browned in spots. Garnish with chives and serve.
Special Equipment
Rimmed baking sheet, large stainless steel or cast iron saucepan
Notes
Yellow onions are your best all-purpose bet for this soup, but a mix of yellow, sweet (e.g., Vidalia), and red onions, as well as shallots, produces an even more complex flavor.

steps.instruction: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large heavy-based pan. Add the onions and fry with the lid on for 10 mins until soft.

Sprinkle in the sugar and cook for 20 mins more, stirring frequently, until caramelised. The onions should be really golden, full of flavour and soft when pinched between your fingers. Take care towards the end to ensure that they don’t burn.
Add the garlic cloves for the final few minutes of the onions’ cooking time, then sprinkle in the plain flour and stir well.
Increase the heat and keep stirring as you gradually add the wine, followed by the beef stock. Cover and simmer for 15-20 mins.
To serve, turn on the grill, and toast the bread. Ladle the soup into heatproof bowls.
Put a slice or two of toast on top of the bowls of soup, and pile on the gruyère. Grill until melted. Alternatively, you can cook the toasts under the grill, then add them to the soup to serve.

technique: 准备15分钟、烹饪55分钟、whole-recipe总用时70分钟，4人份。
用大厚底锅、加盖炒软洋葱10分钟，加糖后经常搅拌20分钟；最后几分钟加入蒜，然后撒面粉拌匀。
加大火力，逐渐边搅边加入白葡萄酒再加高汤，加盖微沸15至20分钟；上火烤至干酪融化，无温度或焗烤分钟数字。

4. 将8片与碗口大小相称的乡村面包烤至酥脆。预热烤箱上火，烤架调至最上层。用另取的黄油涂烤面包片，再用蒜瓣擦至有香气。在4个可入烤箱的汤碗底各舀少量汤汁，各放入1片烤面包（先用其中4片），撒一些磨碎干酪。继续舀入汤和洋葱至接近碗满，再各放1片余下的烤面包，向下轻压至几乎浸入汤中。覆盖余下的干酪，将汤碗放在有边沿的烤盘上。用上火烤至干酪融化且局部呈棕色，撒细香葱，食用。

菜名：法式洋葱汤
- 黄洋葱最适合通用做法；黄洋葱、甜洋葱（如Vidalia）、红洋葱及红葱头混合可产生更复杂的风味，并非必须混用。
- 若没有自制牛高汤，来源建议自制或低钠市售鸡高汤；不要替换成未获同来源推荐的普通市售牛高汤。
- 来源文章说明雪莉酒可选味美思（vermouth）、白葡萄酒，也提到红葡萄酒或波特酒作为替代；未明确各替代用量，只作为可选替代说明，不改变本主配方120毫升干雪莉酒。
- 鱼露可选；苹果醋、雪莉酒用于增加汤底复杂度。

菜名：法式洋葱汤
- 6 tablespoons (90g) unsalted butter, plus more for bread
- 3 pounds (1.4kg) yellow or mixed onions, sliced 1/8 inch thick (see note)
- Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste, divided
- Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste, divided
- 1/2 cup (120 ml) dry sherry (such as Amontillado)
- 2 quarts (1.8L) homemade beef stock or homemade or store-bought low-sodium chicken stock
- 2 sprigs thyme
- 1 bay leaf
- 1 teaspoon (5 ml) Fish sauce (optional)
- 1 teaspoon (5 ml) cider vinegar
- 8 bowl-size slices rustic bread, toasted until crisp
- 1 medium clove garlic
- 1 pound (450 g) Gruyère cheese, grated
- 2 tablespoons freshly minced chives, for garnish
- If browned onion juices on bottom of pot threaten to burn, add 1 tablespoon (15ml) water, scrape up browned bits, and continue cooking.

菜名：法式洋葱汤
1. Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large heavy-based pan. Add the onions and fry with the lid on for 10 mins until soft.
2. Sprinkle in the sugar and cook for 20 mins more, stirring frequently, until caramelised. The onions should be really golden, full of flavour and soft when pinched between your fingers. Take care towards the end to ensure that they don’t burn.
3. Add the garlic cloves for the final few minutes of the onions’ cooking time, then sprinkle in the plain flour and stir well.
4. Increase the heat and keep stirring as you gradually add the wine, followed by the beef stock. Cover and simmer for 15-20 mins.
5. To serve, turn on the grill, and toast the bread. Ladle the soup into heatproof bowls.
6. Put a slice or two of toast on top of the bowls of soup, and pile on the gruyère. Grill until melted. Alternatively, you can cook the toasts under the grill, then add them to the soup to serve.

菜名：法式洋葱汤

- 加大火力，逐渐边搅边加入白葡萄酒再加高汤，加盖微沸15至20分钟；上火烤至干酪融化，无温度或焗烤分钟数字。
